3.0.0.en: The morrow: that is, the morrow of the eighth day, which is the ninth day.

3.0.1.en: The people moved under the leadership of Joshua from Shittim on the ninth day of Nisan and reached the river Jordan after they had prepared provision for the way (ch. 1:10, 11), and they lodged one night at the Jordan, because their crossing of the river was on the tenth day of Nisan (ch. 4:19).

3.1.0.en: Three days after the return of the two spies, who returned on the sixth day of Nisan, the officers, that is, the leaders of the people, went through the midst of them, that is, on the ninth day of Nisan, one day before they crossed the river Jordan.

3.2.0.en: The leaders commanded the people to move behind the ark of the covenant of the Lord, which the priests of the tribe of Levi were carrying. The ark went before the people, making them feel the presence of God who was leading them, so that they would not fear the enemies. This time the priests carried the ark themselves and not the Levites (Num 4:15), because of the seriousness of the situation and to encourage the people.

3.3.0.en: The leaders also commanded the people that there should be a distance between them and the ark of the covenant going before them, which is two thousand cubits, that is, about one kilometer, for the following reasons:

3.3.1.en: 1- That they might feel the fear of God, and so look upon it from afar and be reverent before Him.

3.3.2.en: 2- The existence of a great distance, which is a kilometer, makes the ark clear before the eyes of all the people, so that it leads them easily and they remember that God is their leader in their new life in the Promised Land. This signifies the leading of the Lord for us in life to the new Canaan, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

3.3.3.en: 3- There was a great distance between the ark and them to declare that the Law in the Old Testament gives us the fear of God and prepares us for life with Him, but in the New Testament we draw near to the Holy of Holies and partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

3.3.4.en: 4- The ark of the covenant contained the Ten Commandments, that is, the word of God that leads us in the way of life with Him. It was called the ark of the covenant of the Lord so that they would remember their covenant with the Lord to obey His commandments, and then He would keep them, strengthen them and give them victory over their enemies.

3.4.0.en: Sanctify yourselves: by bathing, washing the clothes, abstaining from marital relations, together with repentance of heart and leaving every sin.

3.4.1.en: Joshua commanded the people to sanctify themselves spiritually and bodily in preparation for witnessing the great work of God in their crossing of the river Jordan.

3.5.0.en: Then Joshua commanded the priests to take up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and pass over before the people, and they did so on the morning of the tenth day of the month of Nisan.

3.5.1.en: May God be a leader for you in the course of your life, so that you remember Him at the beginning of every day as your only goal and seek Him before any work, that He may guide you in all your steps.

3.6.0.en: God declared to Joshua that He would show His greatness before the people as He had magnified Moses before. The beginning of Joshua's magnifying is the dividing of the river Jordan by the hand of Joshua and the crossing of the people, and then He will magnify him after that in his victory over the peoples of the land of Canaan and his dividing of their lands among the tribes of the children of Israel.

3.7.0.en: Joshua commanded the priests who bore the ark that when they reached the river and their feet touched the water, they were to stand still there, because the waters would withdraw from beneath their feet and the river Jordan would be divided, as will come in (v. 15).

3.8.0.en: The Canaanites: the inhabitants of the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, from the descendants of Canaan.

3.8.1.en: The Hittites: a strong people from the descendants of Canaan, whose land was north of Palestine between the Euphrates and Lebanon.

3.8.2.en: The Hivites: from the descendants of Ham, who dwell in cities and work in trade.

3.8.3.en: The Perizzites: from the inhabitants of villages and deserts, who work in farming or herding.

3.8.4.en: The Girgashites: the inhabitants east of the Sea of Galilee.

3.8.5.en: The Amorites: they dwell in the mountains east of the Jordan and are a strong people.

3.8.6.en: The Jebusites: the ancient inhabitants of Jerusalem and its surroundings.

3.8.7.en: Joshua assured them that God would drive out the pagan peoples from before them, because their leader was God, who appeared before them in the ark of His covenant, and God is the God of gods and the Lord of all the earth, so the gods of the nations, who are demons, cannot stand before Him.

3.8.8.en: Let us rejoice that we have from the Lord a promise of the inheritance of the Kingdom, which He will fulfill for us however long the time, according to His true promise. Let us cast away from us every sin or desire, however attractive, and not be troubled if we fall, but rise quickly, confident of God's love for us in preparing the eternal inheritance so that we may reign with Him.

3.9.0.en: A heap: it stands like a wall or a rampart.

3.9.1.en: Joshua commanded the people to choose one man from each tribe for a task that would be announced later, and he told them that when the feet of the priests who bore the ark touched the waters of the river, the waters coming from the north, that is, from the side of the source, would stop in one high heap and become like a wall of water, while the rest of the waters flowing toward their outlet in the Dead Sea continued to withdraw on their way, and so the bed of the river Jordan became dry ground over which all the people crossed.

3.10.0.en: His banks: the shores of the river Jordan and its embankments.

3.10.1.en: So it happened as the Lord promised, and the time was the season of the river's flooding from the melting of the snows of the mountains of Lebanon, which makes the river wide and violent in its flow, and this was at the time of the days of the barley harvest at the end of winter.

3.11.0.en: Adam: the name of a city beside Zaretan, 25 kilometers north of Jericho (Map 1). The sea of the plain: the salt sea, which is the Dead Sea, into which the river Jordan flows from the north. The flow of water in the river Jordan stopped at the city of Adam, which is beside the city of Zaretan, and these are 25 km north of Jericho and of the place where the children of Israel were gathered east of the Jordan. The waters withdrew toward their outlet in the Dead Sea, and the bed of the Jordan became uncovered without water, and all the people crossed from their place, which was later called Bethabara (Jn 1:28), because from it the children of Israel crossed and reached the western side that is called Gilgal (ch. 4:19), and by this they were five miles from the city of Jericho.

3.11.1.en: It is noticed that in the crossing of the Red Sea the waters stood to the right and to the left and the people crossed between them (Ex 14:22), but here the waters stood like a wall on one side only, which is the north side.

3.12.0.en: After the land dried up before the children of Israel and the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord entered into the midst of the river Jordan, all the people passed over and crossed from the east of the Jordan to its west. Two things are noticed in this:

3.12.1.en: 1- The priests did not come out of the river until they were assured that all the people had crossed. This is the duty of the priests in both Testaments, namely caring for the people, baptizing them in the baptismal font, and watching over their walk in the new life.

3.12.2.en: 2- The people crossed the Red Sea forty years before, and those who crossed died, and that crossing was a symbol of Baptism. Now the new generation crosses the river Jordan, which also signifies Baptism, before their entering the new land. Likewise, the sacrament of Baptism is the entrance to all the sacraments and to life in the Church.

3.12.3.en: God chose the time of the flooding of the river Jordan not only to show His miracle in stopping the overflowing waters so that His people might cross, but also because at this time no one expects a great people like this to cross, so their attack on the city of Jericho was a surprise; for in the other days of the year there may be times when the waters of the Jordan are low, so that an ordinary person can cross in water that reaches his knees or a little more.

3.12.4.en: God is able to remove every obstacle from your path, as He stopped the waters in the river Jordan so that His people might cross. So do not be troubled by hindrances, however great, but persevere in prayer and do faithfully all that is in your power, and God is able to remove all obstacles, even if they have lasted a long time, and bring you to the salvation of your soul.

3.12.5.en: Coming up out of the river Jordan

4.0.0.en: After all the people had crossed, the Lord asked Joshua to command twelve men representing the tribes to take twelve stones from beneath the feet of the priests bearing the ark in the midst of the Jordan, and to carry them with them and place them on the western bank of the river Jordan, where they would lodge that night. The twelve men are the number of the tribes of the children of Israel, so that all the tribes might share in glorifying God, who worked with them the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan. The number "12" is also the number of the disciples of Christ, so it signifies the Church in the Old and New Testaments. The number "12" is the product of the number "3", which signifies the Holy Trinity and its work in the believers, and the number "4", which signifies the four directions of the world, that is, the believers in every place; so the number "12" signifies holiness in all the believers.

4.1.0.en: Before the ark of the Lord: that is, toward the ark.

4.1.1.en: In time to come: in the future.

4.1.2.en: What mean ye by these stones?: what is the reason for the presence of these stones.

4.1.3.en: Joshua commanded the twelve men, whom he had chosen from the twelve tribes, to go into the depth of the Jordan, that is, to the ark which the priests were carrying, and take from there twelve stones and transfer them to the western bank of the river Jordan and set them up there as a memorial of the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan, to be a witness to this miracle, and so that the fathers might teach it to their children to strengthen their faith in God.

4.2.0.en: Joshua commanded the people to tell their children the story of the miracle of their crossing of the river Jordan when they asked them about the stone monument made of the twelve stones on the western bank of the Jordan in the place where they lodged, which was called Gilgal (v. 19). After that the chosen men took the twelve stones from the bed of the Jordan and placed them in the place where they lodged on the western bank.

4.3.0.en: Joshua set up twelve stones, which the men had lifted from the western bank of the Jordan, and fixed them in the bed of the river.

4.3.1.en: Do not find the toil of spiritual striving burdensome, whether to rid yourself of your sins or to acquire virtues and persevere in spiritual practices, because this gives you life with God and you enjoy fellowship with Him.

4.4.0.en: The priests who bore the ark remained in the bed of the river Jordan until the chosen men had lifted the stones to the western bank and buried stones in their place in the bottom of the river, and until Joshua had finished charging the people to teach their children as Moses had commanded him before his death, passing on the word of God which He taught Moses. The people crossed the Jordan quickly for the following reasons:

4.4.1.en: 1- Joshua had commanded this so that they would feel seriousness and zeal and begin their new life in the new land with energy.

4.4.2.en: 2- They were eager to reach the new land and possess it.

4.4.3.en: 3- Because their number was large, about 2 million, and with them were children.

4.5.0.en: The priests themselves did not cross until they were assured of the crossing of all the people, confirming the fatherhood of the priest and his concern for all his people.

4.6.0.en: Armed: prepared with weapons of war.

4.6.1.en: Before the children of Israel: going ahead, the men of war from the rest of the tribes.

4.6.2.en: Soldiers also crossed from the two and a half tribes who had received their portion of the land east of the Jordan, to fight with their brethren as the Lord asked of them by the mouth of Moses (Num 32, ch. 1:16-18).

4.7.0.en: Prepared for war: ready for battle.

4.7.1.en: The plains of Jericho: the flat lands of Jericho.

4.7.2.en: The number of those who crossed from the two and a half tribes was about forty thousand persons, to take part in the holy wars west of the Jordan, which the Lord leads. This number is about half the number of the soldiers of the two and a half tribes, whose number is estimated in the text at 110,580 persons, and it is clear that the rest remained in the land east of the Jordan to guard the women, the children and the possessions. All of them encamped in the plains of Jericho.

4.7.3.en: If God is concerned to glorify His holy children, this calls us to glorify them, because glorifying them is glorifying God Himself. So take care to remember your intercessor and glorify him on his feast day and at all times, so that you may learn something from him and God may rejoice in your love for Him.

4.8.0.en: By this the Lord confirmed the greatness of Joshua and the Lord's support of him before all the people, so they respected him as their leader in place of Moses all the days of his life.

4.9.0.en: The ark of the testimony: the ark of the covenant, with the two tablets of the commandments in it.

4.9.1.en: After all the people had crossed the Jordan, the priests bearing the ark came up as the Lord commanded, and the waters returned to flowing and the river filled to its fullest extent. This signifies that the person who submits to the Church and its priests is protected by God from many dangers in the world, but if he moves away from the Church, problems close in on him like the waters of the Jordan, which returned to their flow.

4.10.0.en: The children of Israel came up and crossed the Jordan on the tenth day of the month of Nisan, and by this they completed forty years less five days since they crossed the Red Sea, which they crossed on the fifteenth day of the month of Nisan. They reached Gilgal, whose name means rolling or rolled away, and Joshua called it by this name because God rolled away from them the reproach of Egypt and they arrived at settlement in the Promised Land. Gilgal is located west of the river Jordan beside Jericho and east of it (Map 1).

4.11.0.en: As for the stones that Joshua took from the bed of the river, he set them up in Gilgal, to which they had crossed.

4.12.0.en: Sea of Suph: the Red Sea.

4.12.1.en: Joshua charged the fathers to teach their children throughout the generations the miracle of the crossing of the river Jordan, just as they teach the miracle of the crossing of the Red Sea, when they see the twelve stones set up in Gilgal.

4.12.2.en: Because you are a human being and liable to forget, God calls you to remember His works with you, whether by thanking Him every day in your prayer or by writing down His works and His care for you in spiritual notebooks.

4.13.0.en: Joshua added that setting up the stones in Gilgal has two benefits:

4.13.1.en: 1- When the nations surrounding the Jews see them, they feel the power of the God of the children of Israel, so they fear Him and do not harm His people, as they remember His power in the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan.

4.13.2.en: 2- By the people of God remembering the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan, they fear the mighty God and so keep away from every sin and from the worship of idols.

4.13.3.en: We can arrange the events from the beginning of this book until now in the following order:

4.13.4.en: 1- God commanded Joshua to prepare to depart to cross the Jordan on the third day of Nisan or a few days before that (ch. 1:1).

4.13.5.en: 2- Joshua sent the two spies on the third day of Nisan, and they lodged that night in the house of Rahab (ch. 2:1).

4.13.6.en: 3- The two spies hid three days in the mountain, which were the days 4, 5 and 6 of Nisan (ch. 2:22).

4.13.7.en: 4- The two spies returned to Joshua on the sixth day of Nisan (ch. 2:23).

4.13.8.en: 5- The leaders of the people went through them to gather provision on the seventh day of Nisan and informed them that they would cross the Jordan after three days (ch. 1:10, 11).

4.13.9.en: 6- They journeyed from Shittim to the river Jordan on the ninth day of Nisan and lodged there (ch. 3:1).

4.13.10.en: 7- They crossed the river Jordan on the tenth day of Nisan (ch. 4:19). Spiritual preparation for war
